name: mdm-editor
description: Editor for .mdm files: Markdown, equations and music scores in one rendered, editable document.

mdm.theme.description: MDM editor theme. 'auto' follows the VS Code theme; 'light', 'dark' and 'white' are the editor's own looks, painted by the palettes the extension bakes in whatever VS Code is wearing, 'white' being the light one on a sheet of white paper with the code keeping its slate. The name of any installed colour theme ('Monokai', 'Solarized Light', ...) picks that theme's syntax colours and its side. A name nobody contributes falls back to 'auto'. The toolbar lists them all.

enumDescriptions: Staff lines in gray, Guitar Pro style, so the notes stand out.
Staff lines in the same colour as the notes.
mdm.staffLines.description: Colour of the five staff lines in rendered scores.

enumDescriptions: No background: the score blends into the document, the way an equation does.
Warm paper tint.
Neutral slate tint.
Brass tint, matching the MDM icon.
mdm.scoreFill.description: Fill drawn behind rendered scores. Every option carries a light and a dark value, and the one matching the active theme is used.

enumDescriptions: Scores are centred across the pane, the way display maths is.
Scores start at the left edge of the text.
mdm.scoreAlign.description: Where a rendered score sits across the pane. Only scores narrower than the pane are affected; a full-width one fills the line either way.

enumDescriptions: The YAML header is not shown. It stays on the file and is spliced back on every save.
The YAML header is the first block of the document and is edited in place.
mdm.frontMatter.description: Whether the YAML header is part of the document in the editor. Shown, it is an ordinary block: what is typed in it goes to the file, and deleting it deletes it from the file. A header the hyphenation menu writes into a file that had none comes up hidden whatever this says, so that choosing a language never puts YAML on screen.

enumDescriptions: The outline panel is closed.
The outline panel is open down the left edge, listing the headings.
mdm.outline.description: Whether the outline panel is open. The toolbar button on the left of the bar writes it, so a document reopens with the panel it was left with.

mdm.outlineWidth.description: Width of the outline panel in pixels, as the grip beside it was last dragged to. The editor keeps a column of its own, so a panel wider than the pane allows is narrowed to fit while it is open.

enumDescriptions: Ctrl+D walks whole words, the way VS Code does: a caret in 'score' steps over 'scores'.
Ctrl+D walks every run of the text, inside words too: 'score' also lands in 'scores'.
mdm.multicursorMatch.description: What Ctrl+D (select next occurrence) matches. The toolbar toggle writes it.

enumDescriptions: The page keeps up with the playhead: it keeps the staff system the playhead is walking whole on screen, moving only when part of that band would leave it.
The page is the reader's: a tune plays on wherever it is and nothing scrolls, so a long score can sound while the document is read.
mdm.followPlayhead.description: Whether the page follows the playhead while a tune sounds. On by default. The toolbar toggle writes it.

enumDescriptions: Keep words whole at line endings.
Divide prose words with a visual hyphen when they wrap, in the language the lang field of the YAML header names. A document whose header names no language keeps its words whole.
mdm.hyphenation.description: Word division in prose, off by default. The hyphenation menu in the toolbar sets it for the document it is pressed in, and each document keeps the division it was left on, since the language a document is written in is the document's; this setting is where a document starts. Its first entry keeps words whole, and choosing one of its languages turns division on and writes that language into the lang field of the document's YAML header, adding a header when the file has none, which comes up hidden: the button beside the menu is what shows it. The button is lit while a language is dividing the prose. Hyphens are visual: editing, copying and saving keep the original text. Patterns for German, English, Spanish, French, Italian, Dutch, Polish, Portuguese, Russian and Ukrainian come with the extension; a document in any other language keeps its words whole, and so does a document whose header names no language. An export from the toolbar divides the words the editor divides, in HTML and in PDF.

enumDescriptions: Latin Modern Roman, the face TeX sets a document in, carried inside the extension. Nothing has to be installed and no LaTeX is involved: it is the font on its own, and the equations beside it are already drawn in the same shapes.
The interface font of the system, which is what the rest of VS Code is set in and what Markdown is usually written in.
mdm.textFont.description: The face the text of the document is set in. Code, the numbers in the margin and the toolbar are not affected: they keep the monospace and the sans they have. The toolbar toggle writes it, and an export from the toolbar carries it to the page and to the paper.
